subtype: Approach: having a parent hold the seat and let go [Action]
passage: I'm Nirmala. My cycle was too big for me and I was scared. Papa said, "I'm right behind you, holding the seat. Just pedal and look ahead." I could hear his shoes slapping on the road as he ran. My legs went round and round. The handlebars felt steady. I heard Pallavi, my neighbour, cheering from her gate: "Go, Nirmala!" Then the slapping sounds got quieter. I looked back for one second, and Papa was standing far behind, waving with both hands. I was riding alone! I nearly fell from surprise, but I kept pedalling to the corner.

qa.q: Who cheered for Nirmala from the gate?
What did Nirmala feel on looking back and seeing Papa far behind?
qa.a: Nirmala felt surprised and probably proud and excited, since Nirmala realised the ride was solo. 😊

qa.q: What alternative approach could Nirmala have used if the fear was too big, and why?
qa.a: Nirmala could have practised gliding without pedals first, or asked Papa to let go for a shorter stretch. A gentler start could ease the fear.

qa.q: How might Papa see the moment he let go?
qa.a: Papa waved with both hands from far behind, so Papa was probably happy and proud, and had trusted Nirmala to manage alone.

grounding: A parent holds the seat while Nirmala pedals and lets go unnoticed, and Nirmala finds the cycle is being ridden alone.

subtype: Approach: having a parent hold the seat and let go [Action]
passage:
Mummy, you missed it, so I am writing it down for you before I forget.
This evening in the park, Yamini's papa jogged behind her holding the back of the seat, the way we planned. First round his hand gripped tight; second round only his fingertips. She kept calling, "Don't let go, Papa!" and he kept answering, "I've got you." On the third round he slowed, opened his hand and stopped running. She rode on alone past the swings. Then she looked back, saw him far behind, wobbled and put her feet down, grinning and shaking at once. We had her go twice more, with him letting go sooner each time. Tomorrow we will try starting without his hand at all.
- Alka

qa.q: Where did Yamini ride on alone after her papa let go?
qa.a: She rode on alone past the swings.

qa.q: What was Yamini feeling when she looked back and saw her papa far behind?
qa.a: She was shocked and thrilled at once; the grin shows joy and the shaking shows she was startled to be riding alone.

qa.q: What would you change first if Yamini became too scared to start without the hand?
qa.a: They could let go at the start but have Papa jog alongside without touching, so she feels safe while doing it herself.

qa.q: How might the third round have felt for Yamini's papa?
qa.a: Letting go may have made him nervous, but seeing her ride on past the swings would have made him proud and relieved.

grounding: It shows a girl's father holding the seat while she pedals and then letting go until she rides alone.

subtype: Approach: having a parent hold the seat and let go [Action]
passage:
Tuesday night
Diary, I CAN RIDE. Well, sort of. After school Papa took the blue cycle to the road below the monastery. He ran behind me holding the seat and puffing. I said, "Hold it, hold it!" He said, "Holding!" I pedalled and pedalled and it felt so steady, like being on rails. Then I heard him shout from really far away, "Keep going, Pema!" FAR away. So who was holding? Nobody. Me! I wobbled into the grass when I found out, but I was already past the prayer flags. Deepak uncle from next door clapped from his gate. Papa said, "That's my girl," and his face was all red. Tomorrow I'm going to start by myself.
- Pema

qa.q: Where had Pema already reached when the wobble happened?
qa.a: Pema was already past the prayer flags.

qa.q: How did Pema feel when Papa's shout came from far away?
qa.a: Pema was startled and then thrilled and proud, because the steady feeling had been her own balance all along 🎉

qa.q: What next step would help Pema start alone tomorrow?
qa.a: Pema could begin on the same flat road with Papa jogging beside, not holding, and push off with one foot on a pedal.

qa.q: How did the evening look to Deepak uncle next door?
qa.a: He saw a girl ride past the flags on her own and was happy enough to clap from his gate.

grounding: It shows a girl whose father holds the seat and quietly lets go, so she discovers she is riding on her own.
